(1) earnings announcements are informative and that (2) the information content of an earnings announcement is positively related to the amount of information contained in the announcement and is inversely related to the amount and quality of information available prior to the announcement.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the extent to which earnings possess information content.
the question of how investors perceive earnings to be related to the value of common stocks.
the extent to which investors perceive earnings to have information value.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the earnings announcement has no informational content.

the information content of earnings, as measured by the market's reaction, depends on the extent to which earnings are perceived by investors to possess the following characteristics: a) they are relevant, i.e. they are a measure of performance; b) they are reliable, i.e. the measurement errors are random; and c) they are unbiased, i.e. earnings reflect the underlying performance of the firm.
the information content of earnings, while it is not as great as many would have us believe, is not as small as others have suggested.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the information content of reported earnings, as reflected in common stock price changes, is a function of the quality of the accounting information.
earnings do possess informational content, and that this information content is not completely captured in the current accounting system.
earnings are an important factor in the valuation of common stocks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
earnings are not just a number.
the earnings announcement date has a large impact on the stock price, and the impact is not fully captured by the earnings announcement itself.
the information content of earnings announcements depends on the type of earnings announcements.
